beats.k13: எண்டர்பிரைஸ் மதிப்பு இரண்டாயிரத்து நானூற்றுப் பத்து கோடி ரூபாய், முழுவதும் ரொக்கம். கடன் வழங்குநர், ஒழுங்குமுறை அமைப்பு ஒப்புதல் கிடைத்தால், இரண்டாயிரத்து இருபத்தேழு பிப்ரவரி இருபத்தெட்டுக்குள் முடியும்.
beats.k31: முதல் சோதனை. KPI Green எப்படிப் பணம் செலுத்தும்? இரண்டாயிரத்து நானூற்றுப் பத்து கோடி ரூபாய் ரொக்கம். கடனா, புதிய பங்குகளா, கையிருப்பா என்று ஆவணங்கள் சொல்லவில்லை.

k00.say: KPI Green Energy has agreed to buy five hundred and seven point nine megawatts of working wind farms, for two thousand four hundred and ten crore rupees in cash. It's the company's biggest deal yet, and its first in wind. But the filing leaves out one thing: who pays, and how. By the end of this video you'll know what KPI Green is buying, what it costs, and the three numbers the filings don't give.

k01.say: One note first. This is educational research from the company's own filings, not investment advice. Moat and Margin is not a SEBI registered adviser, and our holdings are disclosed in the description.

k10.say: Chapter one. What KPI Green is buying.

k11.say: On the twenty ninth of September, KPI Green signed a binding offer for one hundred percent of two companies: Alfanar Energy, with three hundred and one point four megawatts, and Netra Wind, with two hundred and six point five. Both run wind farms at Bhuj, in Gujarat's Kutch corridor.

k12.say: Alfanar has been running since March twenty twenty one, Netra since March twenty twenty four. Both sell their power to SECI, the government's Solar Energy Corporation, under twenty five year contracts. On a capacity weighted basis, about twenty one years are left.

k13.say: The price is an enterprise value of two thousand four hundred and ten crore rupees, paid in cash. The deal should close by the twenty eighth of February twenty twenty seven, once lenders and regulators approve.

k14.say: Once it closes, KPI Green's operating power capacity goes from one point one six to about one point six seven gigawatts.

k20.say: Chapter two. The numbers side by side.

k21.say: Start with the price per megawatt. Two thousand four hundred and ten crore, divided by five hundred and seven point nine megawatts, is about four point seven five crore rupees per megawatt. That's our arithmetic, for capacity that's already running.

k22.say: Now the revenue. In the last full year reported, Alfanar's turnover was one hundred and sixty eight point five crore rupees and Netra's one hundred and nine crore. Together, about two hundred and seventy seven crore.

k23.say: Here's the surprising part. KPI Green's own revenue from selling power and services was two hundred and forty eight crore rupees in the whole of last year. The two wind farms it's buying earn more than that.

k24.say: That's because most of KPI Green's revenue still comes from building solar plants for others. In the June quarter, that was five hundred and seventy seven crore of six hundred and ninety four crore. This deal tilts the mix towards long term contracted power.

k30.say: Chapter three. Three things the filings don't say.

k31.say: Check one. How will KPI Green pay? Two thousand four hundred and ten crore rupees in cash, and the filings don't say whether it comes from debt, new shares, or cash in hand.

k32.say: Check two. How much debt comes with the wind farms? Enterprise value includes the targets' own debt. If much of the price is project debt that KPI Green takes over, the cheque is smaller, but the balance sheet carries the loans. The split isn't disclosed.

k33.say: It matters, because on the June quarter call, KPI Green's CFO described the leverage it is comfortable with.

k34.say: That was before this deal. And the company told analysts it prepares a balance sheet only at the half year. So the September half year numbers will be the first real test.

k35.say: Check three. Alfanar's turnover has fallen two years running, from one hundred and ninety two point seven crore to one hundred and sixty eight point five, on the same three hundred and one megawatts. The filings don't say why.

k41.say: The bear case. The funding is unknown. The debt inside the targets is unknown. Alfanar's turnover is falling. And this is a binding offer, not a done deal: definitive documents, lender consents and approvals are still to come.

k42.say: The other side. Both plants are already running, so there's no construction risk. The buyer of the power is a government enterprise, on long contracts. And the deal shifts KPI Green from lumpy construction income towards steady power sales.

k50.say: Chapter five. What it means for the moat.

k51.say: Now the moat. A twenty five year contract with SECI is about as close to locked in revenue as Indian power gets. Moat Score calls this contracted revenue. But a contract locks in the customer, not the margin.

k52.say: KPI Green is not yet scored on our Moat Screener, so there's no score to reveal today. To score this deal, we'd need three things: the tariff on the contracts, the debt inside the targets, and how KPI Green pays for it.

k53.say: So watch three things: the definitive agreements, any funding announcement, and the September half year balance sheet.

k60.say: Every number here comes from KPI Green's own filings. The links are in the description, with the full research note.
